questionText: The stopping sight distance (SSD) on a level road consists of
explanation: Stopping sight distance is the sum of the distance travelled during the driver's perception-reaction time and the braking distance.

questionText: The super-elevation provided on a horizontal curve is mainly intended to
optionB: Counteract the centrifugal force on vehicles
explanation: Super-elevation raises the outer edge of the pavement to counteract the lateral effect of centrifugal force on a vehicle negotiating a curve.
subject: Civil Engineering

questionText: For a vehicle moving on a circular curve of radius R at speed v, the centrifugal force is proportional to
explanation: Centrifugal force is given by F = mv²/R.
subject: Civil Engineering

questionText: The traffic volume passing a point on a roadway is usually expressed in
explanation: Traffic volume represents the number of vehicles passing a specified point or section during a given period and is commonly expressed in vehicles per hour.
subject: Civil Engineering

questionText: Traffic density is defined as the number of vehicles
optionA: Passing a point per unit time
optionB: Occupying a unit length of roadway
explanation: Traffic density is the number of vehicles occupying a unit length of roadway, commonly expressed as vehicles per kilometre.
subject: Civil Engineering

questionText: The fundamental relationship among traffic flow q, density k and speed u is
explanation: Traffic flow is equal to the product of traffic density and average speed, i.e., q = ku.
subject: Civil Engineering

questionText: The California Bearing Ratio (CBR) test is primarily used to evaluate
explanation: The CBR test is commonly used to assess the strength of subgrade soil and other pavement materials for pavement design.
subject: Civil Engineering

questionText: In flexible pavement design, the wheel load is distributed to the lower layers mainly through
explanation: Flexible pavements consist of multiple layers that progressively distribute wheel loads over a larger area to the subgrade.
subject: Civil Engineering

questionText: A traffic signal has a cycle time of 90 seconds. If the effective green time for a traffic movement is 45 seconds, the green ratio is
explanation: Green ratio = effective green time/cycle time = 45/90 = 0.50.
subject: Civil Engineering

questionText: The maximum flow rate that can reasonably be expected to pass through a point on a roadway under prevailing conditions is called
explanation: Traffic capacity is the maximum sustainable rate at which vehicles can pass a given point or section under specified roadway, traffic and control conditions.
subject: Civil Engineering

questionText: The Marshall stability test is primarily used in the design of
explanation: The Marshall method evaluates the stability and flow characteristics of bituminous paving mixtures.
subject: Civil Engineering

questionText: The Passenger Car Unit (PCU) is used in traffic engineering to
optionB: Convert different vehicle types into equivalent passenger cars
explanation: PCU provides a common unit for expressing the effect of different vehicle types on traffic flow relative to a passenger car.
subject: Civil Engineering

questionText: In a rigid pavement, load transfer across transverse joints is commonly provided by
explanation: Dowel bars are smooth steel bars placed across transverse joints to transfer wheel loads between adjacent concrete slabs while allowing longitudinal movement.
